body.statement:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), \(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\), \(\mathrm{ass:mean\text{-}envelope}\), \(\mathrm{ass:second\text{-}moment\text{-}envelope}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:maximal\text{-}effect\text{-}radius}\), the clipped matched-cell occupancy estimator \(\widetilde\tau\) computed from the first \(m_0\) observations satisfies, for \(n\geq 8\),
\[
 E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[(\widetilde\tau-\tau(P))^2\right]
 \leq C_{\epsilon}M^2\left(\sigma^2+\frac1{m_0}+\frac d{m_0^2}\right)
\]
uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\).  The statement is the rescaled real-outcome, bounded-conditional-second-moment form of the published matched-cell occupancy bound.

source.locator: Theorem 3 and its proof in Section C.7, together with the bounded-second-moment extension stated immediately after model (3), arXiv:2405.00118v3
source.verbatim_statement: The bias and variance of \widehat{\tau} are bounded as |\mathbb{E}[\widehat{\tau}-\psi]|\leq\sigma_n+2\exp(-C(\epsilon)n^2/(n\vee d)) and \operatorname{Var}(\widehat{\tau})\lesssim\sigma_n^2+d/n^2+1/n, where C(\epsilon) and the implicit constant depend on \epsilon. The binary nature of Y is assumed primarily for simplicity and is not essential; the rates remain valid when \mathbb{E}[Y^2\mid X=k,A=a]\leq C, which holds with bounded conditional variance.

attestation.note: Source-of-record checked against arXiv:2405.00118v3 HTML, Theorem 3 (lines 315-321), the model-extension paragraph (lines 157-161), and the full proof in Section C.7 (lines 1205-1387), retrieved 2026-09-10. This node is the theorem rescaled from unit/bounded-second-moment constants to M and applied to the first-block sample size m0; no upstream attribution marker appears, and the result is original to the cited work.
